Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the NovaTech Semiconductor Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTech Semiconductor’s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Jian Li, CEO; David Chen, CFO; Sarah Johnson, COO; and Mark Thompson, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Dr. Li.

Dr. Jian Li, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, we've got a detailed breakdown of sales by segment and platform, along with associated margin levels and management commentary. Our Q3 2024 performance showcases a dynamic shift in regional revenue contribution and notable trends within specific technology nodes and application segments. Overall, the company achieved a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year, reaching $2.3 billion, largely fueled by growth in Asia and strategic gains in our IDM and Communication sectors. However, the decline in the European market and the Computer segment requires focused attention and strategic adjustments. This reflects the strength and resilience of our diversified business model.

We also continued to drive improvements through our Net margin and Diluted EPS performance. The company demonstrated solid financial performance in the first three quarters of the fiscal year, highlighted by a healthy net margin and robust diluted EPS figures. Net income attributable to stockholders of the parent company for the first three quarters reached NT$38.71 billion, translating to a diluted EPS of NT$3.12. This signifies a continuation of the positive trend observed in Q3, where net income attributable to stockholders of the parent was NT$14.5 billion, with earnings per ordinary share at NT$1.16. This is underpinned by a company-wide initiative focused on streamlining production processes, reducing waste, and improving supply chain management.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our Gross margin results, where we’ve seen some shifts this quarter. Our gross margin for Q3 2024 came in at 33.8%, a decrease compared to the 35.2% we reported in Q2 2024, and also slightly below our year-to-date gross margin of 33.3%. This decline warrants a closer examination, and David will walk you through the key drivers and mitigating strategies we're employing.

Now I’ll hand it over to David to discuss the financials in greater detail.

David Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Dr. Li, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our wafer sales performance has been quite strong. Wafer shipment grew more than expected, increasing 7.8% sequentially due to a strong demand for 22 and 28 nanometer products, which has contributed meaningfully to our overall revenue and growth. We shipped a total of 4.2 million wafers (12-inch equivalent) this quarter, compared to 3.9 million wafers in Q2 2024.

Second, we saw positive contribution from our overall wafer ASP performance. ASP numbers remain resilient and flattish compared to the previous quarter. The blended ASP didn't see much change, which has enabled more predictable financial planning and allowed us to maintain healthy profitability. Overall ASPs demonstrated remarkable resilience, remaining relatively flattish compared to Q2 2024. The blended ASP experienced minimal deviation, hovering around $1,250 per wafer, a marginal 0.5% decrease from Q2's $1,256.

And although still early, our design win with [Fictional Foundry Name] for our 22nm display driver solution is showing great promise. This quarter saw continued strong performance driven by our strategic partnership with them, a leading advanced node foundry. The collaboration, built on mutual investment in process technology optimization, has allowed us to maintain our competitive edge, particularly in the display driver market.

With that, I’ll turn it to Sarah for a deeper look at operational performance.

Sarah Johnson, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, David.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was the sales performance across different segments, particularly in Asia, which continues to be our dominant market, now representing 65% of total revenue, up from 62% in Q2 2024 and 58% in Q3 2023. This translates to approximately $1.495 billion in revenue generated from the region. The significant growth in Asia is driven by strong demand in China and Southeast Asia, particularly for our embedded solutions used in automotive and IoT applications. We've seen a 20% increase in revenue from our automotive segment within Asia, driven by the adoption of our advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) chips.

Additionally, the resilient ASP numbers have enabled more effective resource allocation and strategic investments in key growth areas.

We’re also seeing early traction in our new fab construction progress in Singapore, where updated processes and advanced technologies are being implemented to enhance our production capabilities. As previously communicated, our strategic investment in expanding our Singapore-based fabrication facility remains a cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy, particularly in addressing the escalating demand for advanced node semiconductors, particularly those supporting AI and high-performance computing applications. The expansion is nearing completion and we anticipate initial production runs to commence in late Q4, with volume ramp-up expected throughout 2024.

Now I’ll pass it to Mark for the tech and product update.

Mark Thompson, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to our Net margin and Diluted EPS improvements, supporting broader adoption and greater operational efficiency. A company-wide initiative focused on streamlining production processes, reducing waste, and improving supply chain management has yielded significant cost savings. Specifically, the implementation of an AI-powered predictive maintenance system in our manufacturing facilities resulted in a 7% reduction in unplanned downtime, translating to approximately NT$500 million in cost savings in the first three quarters.

We’ve also support our design win with [Fictional Foundry Name] by optimizing our 22nm display driver solution, and the performance is truly unparalleled. The 22nm process allows us to achieve a 35% reduction in power consumption compared to competing 28nm solutions. This is crucial for mobile devices and wearable technologies, extending battery life and improving the user experience.

And finally, on the Singapore fab expansion, our new architecture is setting the stage for increased production capacity and enhanced technological capabilities. The physical construction of the fab expansion, which adds approximately 300,000 square feet of cleanroom space, is effectively complete.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the gross margin results and whether you anticipate further fluctuations in the coming quarters?

Dr. Jian Li:
Certainly. The 1.4 percentage point decrease from Q2 to Q3 is primarily attributed to a confluence of factors, with increased depreciation playing a significant role. As mentioned, accelerated depreciation on our newly implemented "Project Phoenix" infrastructure upgrades significantly impacted the bottom line. Project Phoenix is our initiative to modernize our core manufacturing facilities and distribution networks. In Q3 alone, depreciation expenses stemming from Project Phoenix totaled $45 million, compared to $20 million in Q2. While this is a short-term burden, we anticipate significant long-term efficiencies and cost savings from these upgrades, including a projected 8% reduction in energy consumption and a 12% increase in production capacity at our key manufacturing hubs. Comparing to Q3 2023, which had a gross margin of 36.3%, the current 33.8% represents a more significant decline. However, it’s crucial to contextualize this within our broader strategic initiatives. We anticipate that the impact of Project Phoenix on gross margin will peak in Q3 and gradually decline in subsequent quarters as the benefits of increased efficiency and cost savings begin to materialize. We remain committed to delivering long-term value to our shareholders, and we believe that our strategic investments and cost optimization efforts will position us for sustainable growth and improved profitability in the future. We are projecting a gross margin between 34% and 34.5% for Q4 2024.

Analyst 2:
On the wafer sales, how much of the growth is attributable to the 22nm node specifically?

David Chen:
The 22nm node experienced an exceptional quarter. Shipments increased by 12% sequentially, driven by strong demand from the automotive sector for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and electric vehicle (EV) power management ICs. The ASP for 22nm wafers remained relatively stable at $1,215 per wafer, reflecting competitive pricing pressures but also the high value-add of these chips in safety-critical applications. We are seeing increased adoption of our 22ULL (Ultra-Low Leakage) process within this segment, which justifies a slight premium compared to standard 22nm offerings.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to the 22nm display driver solution?

Mark Thompson:
The "unparalleled performance" we highlighted is multifaceted. The 22nm process allows us to achieve a 35% reduction in power consumption compared to competing 28nm solutions. This is crucial for mobile devices and wearable technologies, extending battery life and improving the user experience. Extensive internal testing, in collaboration with key customer [Fictional Mobile Device Manufacturer Name], demonstrated that devices using our 22nm driver achieve on average a 18% longer battery life in mixed-use scenarios compared to devices using competitor solutions. This data was a significant factor in securing several high-volume design wins. It also enables enhanced display capabilities, including higher refresh rates (up to 144Hz in mobile applications), improved color accuracy (covering 98% of the DCI-P3 color gamut), and advanced local dimming capabilities.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on the Singapore fab expansion, is this primarily aimed at increasing capacity for mature or advanced nodes?

Sarah Johnson:
A critical component of this fab expansion is the implementation of advanced automation and process control technologies. We have partnered with Siemens on a comprehensive digital twin initiative that allows us to simulate and optimize wafer flow, identify potential bottlenecks, and proactively address equipment maintenance needs. This initiative is projected to reduce downtime by 12% and improve overall fab efficiency by approximately 5% once fully operational. Furthermore, we are leveraging advanced AI-powered defect detection and classification systems from KLA to enhance quality control and accelerate yield learning. These systems are capable of identifying subtle defects that would be missed by traditional inspection methods, allowing us to rapidly address process variations and optimize manufacturing parameters. The expansion positions us strategically to capitalize on the growing demand for advanced semiconductors in the Asia-Pacific region, which is expected to account for over 60% of global semiconductor consumption by 2025.

Closing

Dr. Jian Li:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
